learning: Baseline (iteration 0) showed line loss at about 0.05 m offset in all 60 trials, with max_error near 0.06 m. Check line_loss_events first: if still above 0, record max_error at the first loss. If steering_oscillation rises without fewer losses, the 16 mm footprint is a suspect. Then tune kp and kd.
notes: Applies the Builder's ±0.05 m spread and 16 mm footprint with the controller unchanged, so only the sensing layout differs from the baseline. Controller is kept fixed to attribute the race change to sensing; the baseline showed every run lost the line at about 0.05 m offset.
rationale: The baseline race (entityR2A, iteration 0, 60 trials) ended every run off_track with one line_loss_event each, max_error about 0.06 m, and progress of only 0.035 to 0.11. Tracking was not the main problem. The robot lost the tape at about 0.045 to 0.05 m offset, then fell back to a fixed search and drifted out. I take the Builder's proposed sensing change as given: sensor spread widens to x = -0.05, -0.025, 0, 0.025, 0.05 at y = 0.04, and footprints grow to 16 mm. I keep the controller unchanged so the race result is attributable to the sensing layout. Sensor weights stay [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2]. The signal is a reading-weighted average of these weights, so it stays within about ±2 at the wider spread, and the same kp and kd keep the response comparable to the baseline. line_loss stays 'last_direction', which still turns the robot toward the side it last saw the tape, and this now matters less because the line should stay visible out to about 0.07 m. base_speed stays at 1.6, and ki stays at 0 to avoid windup on bends. I measure line_loss_events, max_error and rms_error, plus progress and completion, so the next iteration can tell whether the spread fixed the failure or whether the controller now needs tuning.
